title: Course Skill Adherence — the rules THIS course is written under
description: A course carries SKILLS: instructions authored by its owner and approved before they take effect (src/skills.py) — 'show the snippet before explaining it', 'never teach class components', 'one worked-example pattern throughout'. They are what makes a React course different from an Operating Systems one, and nothing else in this suite measures them: the other 25 sets are the house rules that hold for every course. ONE dimension covers every course, parameterised by that course's own skills — a set per skill, or per course, would mean re-authoring the suite each time a course is created.
criterion: Every approved skill governing this course is honoured by the document. Skills carrying a machine-checkable assertion are checked exactly, by the same code the generation gate uses, so the eval and the gate cannot disagree. The rest — the ordinary case, since a brief is written in prose — are weighed by the judge, which is given the brief verbatim and required to quote the line and the text that breaks it. The two halves are combined as the MINIMUM: a document cannot pass by satisfying the checkable skills while ignoring everything else its course owner wrote. A course with NO approved skills is not scored here at all, because it has not said what it requires.

rubric.5: Every skill is honoured — the checkable ones exactly, the prose ones in spirit.
rubric.4: Honoured throughout, with one place where a prose skill is followed loosely.
rubric.3: One checkable skill is violated, or one prose skill is clearly not followed.
rubric.1: Several skills are violated, or the document ignores its course's own brief.
